themes.theme: Search utility is the real value prop — and it's landing
themes.summary: All 5 partners are actively querying their archives to solve real-world tasks: Chloe pulling city-specific travel details into blog posts, David retrieving architecture decisions, Jordan surfacing missed action items. Search queries jumped from 3.5 to 4.8 per user per week. The product has shifted from passive journal to interactive memory layer, and partners feel it.

themes.theme: 4 of 5 partners stated concrete willingness to pay
themes.summary: Chloe ($60/yr), David ($10/mo), Jordan ($4.99/mo), and Aris (~$50–100/yr) all gave unprompted price anchors. Maya is the only partner without a stated WTP on record. This is unusually strong signal at Week 8 — but the numbers need to harden into actual conversion before G4 is locked.

themes.theme: Zero friction surfaced across all 5 partners — a suspicious pattern
themes.summary: Every single piece of feedback in this cohort is positive, and every feature request is explicitly framed as cosmetic or trivial (fonts, cassette tape UI, confetti animations, haptic patterns). No partner reported a miss, a bug, an accuracy failure, or a workflow gap. Universally frictionless feedback from 5 diverse users is a data quality signal, not a product quality signal — it likely means the feedback collection method isn't pulling hard enough.

must_fix_for_g4: Collect explicit stated WTP from Maya — she is the only partner without a price anchor, and G4 needs paying signal across the cohort, not just 4 of 5.

Run a structured friction interview (not a survey or form) with at least 2 partners to surface real failure modes — the current feedback loop is returning zero criticism, which means the questions aren't hard enough.
Get at least one partner to convert from stated WTP to an actual payment or signed LOI before G4 — verbal anchors are necessary but not sufficient.
nice_to_have_post_launch: Serif font option for AI-generated summary displays (Aris).
Time-of-day personalized home screen greeting copy — 'Ready for a brain dump?' style variants (Chloe).
Retro cassette tape / 90s dictaphone skin for the active recording screen (David).
Configurable haptic feedback pattern on record button press — double-tap or lighter tick options (Jordan).
Sparkle / confetti micro-animation when a new memory card finishes processing (Maya).
next_sprint_brief: Strong week — the scorecard is moving in the right direction and 4 of 5 partners gave you unprompted price anchors, which is rare at Week 8. Your one non-negotiable this sprint is Maya: get on a call, ask her directly what she'd pay, and log it. Beyond that, the feedback cohort returned zero criticism across five diverse users, and that is a yellow flag — not because the product is bad, but because your feedback collection method isn't stress-testing it. Before G4, run at least two partners through a structured friction interview where you ask them to recall the last time Eterna gave them a wrong answer, missed a tag, or made them do extra work to get what they needed. Finally, pick one of the four WTP partners — Chloe or David are your strongest signals — and ask them to convert: put a Stripe link in front of them this week and see if the stated $60/year or $10/month holds under a real payment prompt.
g4_readiness_rationale: The scorecard is live, all 5 partners are active, D30 retention is at 62.5% and trending up from 58.3%, and 4 of 5 partners gave concrete price anchors — the master metric (D30 retention) is exceeding its own target. The remaining blockers before a confident G4 are specific and closeable: Maya needs a WTP conversation, the feedback loop needs sharpening to surface real friction, and at least one stated WTP needs to convert to actual payment.
scorecard_gaps_flagged: Time-to-first-value (TTFV): how quickly a new partner records their first memo and receives a processed summary — critical for understanding onboarding quality.
Activation rate on search: what % of partners used search in their first 7 days vs. only after week 3 — distinguishes immediate vs. delayed value discovery.

Transcription / summarization accuracy rate: no quantitative error rate is tracked; given accuracy is the core promise, this should be a logged metric (e.g. % of summaries rated accurate by user, or thumbs-down events).
Conversion funnel: stated WTP → payment prompt shown → converted. Currently only stated WTP is tracked; actual conversion is absent.
Memo abandonment rate: % of recording sessions started but not completed — could surface silent friction the qualitative feedback is missing.
Tag acceptance rate: % of AI-generated tags that partners keep vs. delete or override — a proxy for model quality in the semantic indexing layer.
